newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Gulf rigs up two at 168 in the week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Gulf rigs up two at 168 in the week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 964 as of Friday, down one from the prior week and 176 above the year-ago total of 788, Baker Hughes Inc. reported.
The number of rigs drilling on land fell by two to 816, while rigs working offshore rose two to 124. The number of rigs active in inland waters dipped one to 24.
Among the individual states, the biggest changes occurred in Oklahoma, which was down by 18, California and Texas, which were up by eight, and Wyoming, which was up by four.
The Gulf of Mexico rig count was up by two at 120.

A total of 368 rigs were exploring for crude oil, down 12 from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas rose by 10 to 593, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects rose by one to three.
There were 213 rigs drilling directionally, 71 drilling horizontally and 680 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by 41 to 376, versus 299 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
Separately, Offshore Data Services said there were 168 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of Friday, up two from the period ending July 7.
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 175, was 96.0 percent.
The number of working rigs in the European/Mediterranean area was unchanged at 110 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 113, a utilization rate unchanged at 97.3 pct.
The worldwide rig count was up two at 578 out of a total fleet of 604, with an unchanged utilization rate of 95.7 percent.
